recognize_zh: 超活體染色（New Methylene Blue）下，箭頭所指的三顆紅血球表面佈滿均勻細小的藍色點狀沉澱，像高爾夫球表面凹洞（golf ball appearance），為 HbH 包涵體；周圍另有含網狀結構的網狀紅血球作為對照。
features: Three red cells (arrows) covered by numerous fine, evenly distributed blue-green granular inclusions giving a golf ball appearance
Affected cells round and normal to slightly small in size
Several reticulocytes with irregular blue filamentous/granular reticulum for comparison
Background red cells with mild anisopoikilocytosis
No large solitary membrane-bound inclusions (Heinz bodies) in this field
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear with supravital New Methylene Blue stain (high power) shows occasional red cells uniformly studded with numerous fine, evenly spaced blue inclusions, producing a golf ball appearance consistent with hemoglobin H precipitates. Several reticulocytes with coarse, irregular reticulum are also present and serve as contrast. Background red cells show mild anisopoikilocytosis. In the setting of myelodysplastic syndrome, findings are consistent with acquired HbH disease (alpha-thalassemia-MDS, often ATRX-mutated), which may be missed by routine HPLC.

ddx.vs: Reticulocytes show an irregular filamentous or clumped network concentrated in part of the cell rather than evenly spaced fine dots covering the whole cell.
Heinz bodies are one to few larger round inclusions attached to the membrane, whereas HbH inclusions are numerous, fine and diffusely distributed.
Morphology is identical, so distinguishing congenital HbH disease from acquired ATMDS relies on age, family history, alpha-globin gene deletion analysis, and MDS features with ATRX mutation.
Basophilic stippling is visible on Romanowsky stains as ribosomal RNA dots, whereas HbH inclusions require supravital staining and incubation.
